quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: In a turn, you should roll on the throttle to:

options.text: Keep your speed steady or increase it slightly to help stabilize the motorcycle.
Slow down to have more control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or increase it slightly to help stabilize the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: When turning, roll on the throttle to keep your speed steady or increase it slightly. This helps stabilize your motorcycle.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A motorized bike with less than 45 cubic centimeters displacement:

options.text: Cannot be used on public roads.
Must be ridden on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be used on public roads.
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, motorized bikes with engines under 45 cubic centimeters or tire diameters under 14 inches cannot be used on public roads.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on good pavement, leave it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you stop on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when holding the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly. Keep your knees against the gas tank to balance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
Stop completely and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation to stay together with safe distance between riders is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close while giving each rider enough safe distance.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard on the road, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Slow down or speed up as needed. Change your lane position or direction to stay safe.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together to see better.
Turn only your shoulders, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you will be slowing down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will be slowing down quickly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as bright as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so other drivers notice you are slowing down. This is especially important when you slow faster than expected.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark. Use at least three seconds of following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when turning or going through a curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when turning or going through a curve.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and your bike lean the right way.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It connects to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you apply the rear brake pedal, it connects the front and rear brakes. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders must wear eye protection. Is this required?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear proper eye protection.

questions.question: Another vehicle is passing you from behind. Which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon, which is also unsafe.

questions.question: What fraction of motorcycle and car collisions are caused by drivers not yielding the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume a driver will yield, even if they are legally required to do so.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while braking. What should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then re-apply it.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of the lane provides traction. When is this NOT true?

options.text: Only when you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually has enough traction for safe riding, but not when it rains. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.
